text:
alex_support: Hi @customer_jp — saw your ticket about the embeddings endpoint 500s and the dim-mismatch errors. Can you paste a minimal request and the exact error? :eyes:

customer_jp: Thanks. Repro steps: we upgraded our client lib and started sending the same payloads. Now ~5% of calls return 500 with 'InvalidEmbeddingDimension: expected 1536 but got 768'. No schema changes on our side. Example payload: `{\"input\": \"hello\"}` hitting route `POST /v1/embeddings` model `embed-large-v2`.

alex_support: Got it. Two quick hypotheses: 1) mixed model variants getting coalesced in dynamic batching so different model dims interleave, 2) a client-side config accidentally toggled a smaller model for a subset of requests. Can you confirm your model id is always `embed-large-v2` and any A/B routing?

customer_jp: We pin the model id in the call, no A/B on our end. No recent deploys except the client lib upgrade.

chun_engineer: Jumping in — can you share a raw request id from a failing call and the full server error blob? I want to correlate with batch logs.

customer_jp: Sure: request_id=rid_2026_aa77, timestamp=2026-02-18T16:42:07Z. Error body: `{\"error\":\"InvalidEmbeddingDimension\",\"expected\":1536,\"got\":768,\"batch_id\":\"b-7f2\"}`

jen_oncall: Looking at runtime logs for b-7f2 — I see this entry in the batcher log: `coalescer: merged 3 reqs -> model_variant: embed-large-v2, embed-small-v1` followed by `dispatch to device gpu-12`. So two different variants got merged into the same batch. That explains dim mismatch. This should not happen for model-pinned requests.

mira_sre: Are clients allowed to request model aliases? We recently rolled out variant fallback that can route to `embed-small-v1` if capacity constrained. Might be a routing policy bug where pinning isn't enforced for certain legacy tokens.

alex_support: Oof. That would explain it — if the token had a fallback policy and the coalescer combined requests across fallback-compatible variants, the batch would have mixed dims. Severity: customer is seeing embedded errors and tail latency spikes when batches get rejected and retried.

chun_engineer: Quick mitigation I can push: temporarily disable dynamic batching for routes that have variant fallbacks OR enforce model-variant strictness at the coalescer boundary. Which is faster?

mira_sre: Short-term: we can flip `dynamic_batching:false` for the customer's route via config flag (non-disruptive, immediate). Longer-term: change the coalescer key to include the model_variant_id (not just model family + route). That requires a small change and a canary rollout.

alex_support: I patched the customer's route to disable dynamic batching and forced strict model variant matching. Can you monitor for errors, @customer_jp?

customer_jp: After the patch, the errors dropped to 0. Tail latency improved too. Thanks. Any chance this causes higher P99 on our side because we lose batching?

chun_engineer: Yes you may see higher token cost/latency for small requests. Mitigations: 1) pin to a single variant that matches your expected dim (1536) and keep dynamic batching on once we fix coalescer. 2) tune `coalesce_window_ms` to 15-25ms to balance latency vs batching. We can run a quick AB.

jen_oncall: Filed ENG ticket INF-3248 to change coalescer key and add a safety assert to refuse mixed-dim batches. I'll schedule a canary deploy to eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

infra-bot: Deploy started for INF-3248-canary -> eu-west-1 at 2026-02-18T17:12:00Z.

mira_sre: Post-deploy plan: observe coalescer metrics (batches/sec, mixed_variant_rejections), and run a synthetic load that mixes pinned and fallback requests to ensure no regression.

alex_support: Closing loop with customer: INF-3248 created, immediate mitigation applied (dynamic batching disabled for their route), recommending model-variant pin to avoid cost/latency regressions. @customer_jp please reopen if you see any recurrence. :thumbsup:

customer_jp: Confirmed stable for 24h. Appreciate the fast response and the clear mitigation steps.

chun_engineer: Follow-ups: we'll add an automated alert if coalescer ever logs an attempted mixed-variant merge, and add a small unit test in the coalescer to prevent regressions.

alex_support: Thanks team — marking resolved for now.
